## Report the denominator first

`bench_transition_metrics()` joins predictions to public outcomes in SQL.
It returns one metric row and a count for each source outcome state.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  O[Public outcomes] --> E[Select the declared evaluation task]
  E --> J[Join predictions by unit and context]
  P[Probability scores or abstention] --> J
  J --> C[Coverage and excluded outcome counts]
  J --> M[Scored-subset metrics]
```

## Keep two questions separate

| Task | Positive | Negative | Excluded |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resolved_direction` | `to_pathogenic` | `to_benign` | All other outcomes |
| `observed_pathogenic_resolution` | `to_pathogenic` | Every other observed outcome state | None |

The second task retains every supplied baseline VUS. A missing, retired, or changed-context record remains in that denominator.
Its zero label means no observed pathogenic resolution in this comparison, not biological benignity or complete follow-up.
Report the separate outcome counts to show loss of follow-up and context changes.
The first task conditions on later resolution. It does not measure resolution probability for all baseline VUS.

## Missing predictions stay visible

Missing rows and NULL scores are abstentions. They remain in the eligible population count.
`coverage` reports the scored fraction. `recall_eligible` counts unscored eligible positives as unrecovered.

Precision, recall, balanced accuracy, F1, Brier score, ROC AUC, and average precision use scored eligible rows.
Their names end in `_scored`. An undefined rate is NULL, not a perfect score.
Average precision groups equal scores before accumulating recall. It is not trapezoidal PR area.

## Use it

This example needs caller-owned outcome and prediction relations. Rendering does not execute it.

```r
result <- bench_transition_metrics(
  con, outcomes = "vus_outcomes", predictions = "vus_predictions",
  task = "resolved_direction", threshold = 0.5
)
result$outcome_counts
result$metrics
```

Predictions require `unit_id`, `condition_id`, `submitter_id`, and `score`.
Keep context keys as VARCHAR. Use probabilities in [0,1], or NULL.
Source outcomes stay outside prediction inputs.

Tests cover ties, missing predictions, empty scores, single-class subsets, every outcome state, invalid values, and denominator changes between tasks.
These tests do not claim measured public-cohort accuracy.
